Ivy: Heads-up: PartnerCloud just raised a billing dispute. They say several customers got negative adjustments after we applied their compacted 'summary' payloads. Ticket: https://partnercloud.help/TK-771
Marcus: negative adjustments? like credits appearing suddenly?
Ivy: yep. For some accounts we applied a negative delta that exceeded the original usage for that window, ending up with a net negative billed quantity.
Diego: do we have a sample payload?
Ivy: pasted redacted example from partner: ```{"partner_id":"partnercloud","window":"2026-03-05T10:00:00Z","summaries":[{"customer":"pcust-19","delta":-120,"reason":"correction"}] ,"signature":"..."}```
Marcus: oof. they send deltas in summaries and expect us to apply them against prior raw events. We currently apply summaries eagerly as absolute adjustments without bounding, so negative deltas can over-correct when prior events are missing.
Diego: root cause guess: PartnerCloud compacts old raw lines into summaries and deletes the originals on their side. If our ingest missed the original (late delivery) we see a corrective delta without base usage.
Ivy: partner confirmed they do aggressive compaction after 48h to reduce S3 costs. they assume marketplace will store originals.
Marcus: quick mitigation: treat summary deltas as "provisional" if there is no matching prior window record. Don't mutate ledger; instead create a pending adjustment that requires reconciliation within 14 days.
Diego: agree. Technical plan: 1) Change summary handler so that if delta < 0 and no matching prior usage_id found -> insert pending_adjustment(row) and emit reconciliation alert. 2) If partner later replays raw events, auto-apply and clear pending.
billing-bot: Query queued: SELECT customer_id, SUM(delta) FROM marketplace_summaries WHERE partner='partnercloud' AND delta < 0 AND received_at >= '2026-02-01' GROUP BY customer_id; estimated rows: ~32 customers with non-zero negative totals
Ivy: for affected customers we'll need to open invoices with "pending credit" flag and not auto-issue refunds until manual review.
Marcus: policy decision: do we expose a SLA requiring partners to retain raw events for 30 days or accept liability for over-crediting? We should push for retention requirement in marketplace onboarding.
Diego: enforcement idea: extend the ingestion contract to require either (a) retain raw events 30d OR (b) include full snapshot (absolute usage) in any corrective summary. That way we can reconcile without originals.
Ivy: partner relations: I'll draft amendment language and present to PartnerCloud. Also need to surface these impacted customers and propose temporary suspend of auto-refunds.
partner-relations-bot: Note logged: partnercloud-contact@partnercloud.com CC: marketplace-ops@redwood.com
Marcus: operational tasks: Diego implement provisional flag + pending_adjustment table; billing team to show "pending credits" in invoices UI; Ivy coordinate with partner on retention clause and timeline; billing-bot generate affected customer list and mark invoices as review_needed.
billing-bot: Action items recorded: ["Diego: provisional summary flow PR","Ivy: partner amendment + comms","Billing: show pending credits in UI","billing-bot: affected customer list"]
Diego: I'll aim to open PR today that prevents auto-application of negative deltas when no anchor exists; includes unit tests for replay path.
Ivy: PartnerCloud asked for a replay API to push originals for up to 21 days. They can do 21d for enterprise customers, 7d for all others. Can we accept 21d for enterprise?
Marcus: yes but require signed manifests when >7d. Also enforce HMAC signatures on replays and throttle replays to avoid DOS.
Ivy: next sync: internal triage at 11:00, and I'll send partner note with proposed 21d enterprise / 7d standard and draft retention clause. Thanks all.
